new_statements.quote: Phonetically, the stress pattern for ‘700’ and ‘800’ also differs, with primary stress on the initial syllable of [hóraluluŋat], but on the second syllable of [holúluŋat], and the final syllable of [hosaŋát].
new_statements.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Counting in the Admiralty Islands. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 39: 19-55. (Glottolog ref 586201.)
new_statements.locator: LLM 39 (2021) p.40 (p.23, lines 19-20); companion remark p.35 (p.18): '.. the stress pattern differs, but this difference is in the secondary stress, not the primary stress: [hóralùŋuh] ‘70’, [hórùluŋuh] ‘80’.'
new_statements.relation_note: Two explicit remarks with stress-marked phonetic forms. p.35: 'the Ahus forms for '70' and '80' are both quadrisyllables that in their segmental phonology differ only in a single vowel.. Evidently to prevent this from happening, the stress pattern differs, but this difference is in the secondary stress, not the primary stress: [hóralùŋuh] '70', [hórùluŋuh] '80'.' p.40: 'Phonetically, the stress pattern for '700' and '800' also differs, with primary stress on the initial syllable of [hóraluluŋat], but on the second syllable of [holúluŋat], and the final syllable of [hosaŋát].' No general stress rule, nothing on phonemic status; all other Ahus forms are unmarked.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule stated. In Blust's transcriptions primary stress is initial in '70', '80' and '700', on the second syllable in '800' and on the final syllable in '900'; he presents the differences as keeping near-identical numerals apart. Stress position in Ahus words is thus recorded as variable across these forms; the paper does not say whether Ahus stress is predictable in general.
new_statements.secondary_stress: transcribed: '70' [hóralùŋuh] vs '80' [hórùluŋuh] differ only in the place of secondary stress (third vs second syllable)
new_statements.exceptions: none beyond the five numerals discussed
new_statements.identity_note: Ahus = the Hus Island speech of Andra-Hus [anx]; Blust's Feb-May 1975 Admiralties survey data ('Ahus, Hus village (Balthasar Kipit)', p.21 fn.1) [name in source: Ahus (Hus village; speaker Balthasar Kipit, 1975); pages 21 fn.1 (speakers), 27-49 passim (numeral tables), 35 and 40 (stress remarks)]
